markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Appended-mask prediction uses only preceding events, whereas interior reconstruction can exploit later events. Increasing terminal supervision tests this mismatch directly. (2) Users report stale-interest recommendations and weak, broadly related matches. Training on chronological prefix endpoints could emphasize the context preceding an actual choice; improvements remain hypothetical. (3) Industrial and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile training margins (−0.2267 and −0.0479). These identify ranking weaknesses, without establishing their cause or held-out impact.

**Related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes last-item masking. The contribution here is a controlled supervision experiment, not a new masking principle. (2) [Petrov and Macdonald](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivate task-aligned sampling. Their findings do not establish an optimal random-prefix schedule here. (3) [Klenitskiy and Vasilev](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) highlight loss and sampling confounds. Negative count and objective should therefore remain fixed during the masking experiment.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Intervention | Intended gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision alignment | Fixed terminal-mask mixture | Interior recovery versus next-item prediction |
| Temporal representation | Learned relative-position attention bias | Distinguishing persistent and current interests |
| Ranking supervision | Moderately hard negative sampling | Weak positive–negative separation |

Scores below are prospective judgments, not measured results. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed terminal mixture | 3: controlled adaptation; established principle | 8: reusable baseline; gains uncertain | 7: targets current context; no compatibility evidence | 7: endpoint ranking; causality unproven | 3: sampler change; weighting needs care |
| Learned positional bias | 5: flexible relevance; familiar mechanism | 7: preserves older signals; may overfit | 7: contextual relevance; cannot establish ownership | 5: changes attention; sensitivity direction unavailable | 6: small parameters; writer changes required |
| Moderate-hard negatives | 4: focused ranking; established sampling | 7: targets difficult distinctions; false negatives | 5: sharper rankings; relevance remains uncertain | 8: addresses margins; training-only evidence | 6: same network; proposal correction needed |

## Selected experiment: fixed terminal-mask mixture

At 10% progress, select the simplest controlled intervention: allocate 50% of sequence examples to terminal masking and retain baseline random masking otherwise. For a terminal example, sample a training-history cutoff, hide its target with the reserved mask, and discard every later event. Retain bidirectional attention over the prefix.

This explicitly targets **older interests treated as continuing demand** and **weak, broadly related matches** by learning choices from their preceding context. It also targets weak masked-target separation through prediction-aligned supervision. None of these improvements is established; compatibility and redundancy remain unresolved.

Keep loss, negatives, optimizer, and per-example loss normalization fixed. Preserve all four routes, seeds 0/42, 200 batches/epoch, and maximum 200 epochs. Save one checkpoint/category; select using host macro validation HR@10. Record sampler provenance and preserve diagnostic APIs. Read the final nonpadding mask position and keep predictor loading consistent.

idea.description: Test a fixed 50% mixture of random-prefix terminal-mask examples and baseline random-mask examples within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Train exactly one independent model per category and retain appended-mask inference.
idea.motivation: Terminal examples remove the future context available in interior reconstruction and align supervision with prediction. This could reduce stale-interest and weak broad-similarity recommendations while improving endpoint ranking. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show weaker training-exposed margins, but neither the causal explanation nor validation improvement is established.
idea.implementation_notes: Change only the masking-example sampler and the normalization needed to maintain equal per-example weighting. Preserve the baseline loss, negative count and distribution, optimizer, architecture, and user-sampling distribution. Draw cutoffs exclusively within supplied training histories, requiring at least one preceding interaction. Terminal examples contain the preceding prefix and reserved mask, never the target ID or later interactions; truncate the prefix to L-1 and left-pad. Random-mask examples retain the corrected baseline behavior, with supervised targets hidden. Average supervised-position losses within each example before averaging examples, applying the same normalization to the control. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and at most 200 epochs. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Load exactly one checkpoint per category. Preserve ModelView, log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Record provenance separately without changing the four-tuple loader contract. Diagnostics must distinguish terminal and interior training margins and report unavailable checks honestly. The predictor writer must reproduce the trained architecture and appended-mask construction. Find the last nonpadding index from positions, never count-1. Do not infer unavailable compatibility, ratings, review text, or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
Set preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42.
For each required category:
    Initialize the supplied corrected BERT4Rec.
    For each epoch, at most 200:
        For each of exactly 200 batches:
            Sample training users using the baseline distribution.
            For each sampled history h:
                If len(h)>=2 and seeded_uniform()<0.5:
                    j = seeded_uniform_integer(1, len(h)-1)
                    prefix = h[max(0, j-(L-1)):j]
                    sequence = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], L)
                    positive = zeros(L); positive[L-1] = h[j]
                    negative = baseline_negative_sample(h[j], history=h)
                    Record cutoff and mask provenance separately.
                Else:
                    sequence, positive, negative = corrected_baseline_masking(h)
                Compute unchanged loss at valid supervised mask positions.
                Reduce positions to one mean loss per example.
            Backpropagate the mean example loss through this single network.
    Save the selected single checkpoint and matching configuration.
Write the matching category-routed predictor.
For prediction:
    sequence = left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    index = max(position where sequence[position] != PAD)
    scores = model.predict_score(features[index], candidate_items)
Obtain selection scores only from the unchanged host validation evaluator.

originality.positive: Provides a controlled, diagnosis-motivated test of random-prefix endpoint supervision under the corrected BERT4Rec protocol.
originality.negative: Last-item masking is already part of BERT4Rec; the mixture is an experimental adaptation rather than a novel backbone or objective.

future_potential.positive: A clean result would establish a useful foundation for subsequent temporal-representation or ranking-supervision experiments.
future_potential.negative: The 50% mixture is a proposed setting without benchmark-specific evidence, and endpoint supervision cannot establish item compatibility or incremental usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily changes sampling while preserving architecture and inference interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct cutoff construction, target hiding, loss normalization, provenance, and predictor consistency require careful verification.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Includes last-item masking to align training with terminal-mask recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish the optimal terminal-mixture frequency for the pinned four-category benchmark.
Makes terminal supervision an established baseline component rather than an original contribution here.

related_work.title: Petrov and Macdonald (2022), recency-sampling research
contributions: Motivates examining task alignment and convergence costs of general masked reconstruction.
limitations: Does not establish gains from the proposed random-prefix BERT4Rec mixture on this benchmark.

related_work.title: Klenitskiy and Vasilev (2023), sequential-recommendation loss comparison
contributions: Highlights the importance of loss and negative sampling in sequential-recommendation comparisons.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed terminal-mask mixture.
Motivates controlling these factors rather than changing them simultaneously.
